notes:
I couldn't do the research, so I don't have any notes for you yet.

I tried to load six pages at once: Enduring Word, Precept Austin, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub, and the NET Bible notes on Daniel 4. My code to read the results failed. When I tried to fix it, the tool said I'd used all my calls for this turn. None of those pages came back in a form I could read, and I haven't been able to search or fetch anything since.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give the URL for every point, and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written anything from memory, and none of the three sections (traditional reading, Protestant differences, other views) have notes.

**Next time** I can start again in a new turn, reading pages one at a time so a single error can't block the whole batch. This is the plan:

1. **Main verse-by-verse sources:** Enduring Word, Precept Austin, and Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub or StudyLight.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:**
   - Wesley's Explanatory Notes (wesley.nnu.edu) for the Methodist view.
   - Ligonier, Desiring God and The Gospel Coalition for Reformed and Baptist views.
   - Spurgeon's sermons, especially on verses 34–37.
   - Lutheran sources (LCMS, 1517.org).
   - Ryle or other Anglican writers if I can find them on CCEL.
   - Likely debates include whether Nebuchadnezzar was truly converted (vv. 34–37), what the "watchers" are (vv. 13, 17), and whether verse 27 suggests good deeds earn favour.
3. **Other views:**
   - NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship, such as the Nabonidus theory and the Aramaic text.
   - New Advent, Catholic.com and OCA for Catholic and Orthodox readings, including Jerome's commentary and the almsgiving reading of verse 27.
   - Got Questions and similar sites for popular teaching.

Just reply "continue" and I'll start.
